B(t)=int_0^t s gives q/sqrt(1-q^2)=(q0/sqrt(1-q0^2))exp(-(r-c)B/2), with q0=0 invariant. Positivity and L=s+(a/b)z yield a global upper bound, and B cannot remain finite because that would force z->0 and then positive logistic recovery of s, contradiction. The B-change-of-variable reduces the accumulated penalty to elementary log integrals, giving -log|q0| for c>r unequal, -0.5log(1-q0^2) for r>c, and zero in invariant cases, absolutely convergent. Perturbed Volterra Lyapunov functions with integrable delta=d(q)-d_inf give int(s-s_inf)^2<infinity; uniform continuity and bounded derivatives prove s->s_inf and z->z_inf even on the invasion equality boundary. Independent symbolic derivative algebra and numerical IVP c=2,r=1,b=1.25,a=1 show unequal predator limit 0.2 vs equal predator extinction and correct log penalty; finite IVPs are diagnostic.
